subject: Buffer allocation, SLOs & failure-mode scenarios for ZenTech private GPU pool

Subject: Buffer allocation, SLOs & failure-mode scenarios for ZenTech private GPU pool

Hi Vivek / Marissa,

Attached is our traffic profile export (CSV) and a short note on expected workload shape. We're planning a VPC/private deployment of our inference workload and need Redwood's sizing recommendation so we can commit to a capacity window. Key asks:

- Target SLOs: p95 latency < 120ms, p99 latency < 250ms (inference-only).
- Typical context length: 4k tokens. 75% of requests are generation with an average of ~180 tokens output.
- Steady-state target: 200 req/s. Peak bursts up to 700 req/s for periods of 3–10 minutes.
- Expected retention: KV cache warming during business hours matters.

Can you run an initial buffer-allocation proposal (including recommended warm pool size and burst absorb capacity) and highlight any network/egress limits we should be aware of on private deployments? Ops is CC'd for egress/IP whitelisting and testing windows.

Attachments: zentech-traffic-profiles.csv

Thanks,
Anna Ramirez
Head of ML Ops — ZenTech Labs
anna@zentech.com

--

(Replying parties: please include a short runbook or checklist for canary steps and an ops contact for egress rules.)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Buffer allocation, SLOs & failure-mode scenarios for ZenTech private GPU pool

Anna — thanks for the export, that's very helpful. Initial read and high-level proposal below (quick, conservative numbers while we validate with your real traces):

On Sun, May 9, 2027 at 15:12 Anna Ramirez <anna@zentech.com> wrote:
> Attached is our traffic profile export (CSV) and a short note on expected workload shape.

Summary proposal (short):
- Base steady capacity: size to sustain 200 req/s at target tail SLOs. From the profile, that maps roughly to 4 H100-equivalent GPUs (model/sequence-dependent); see attached sizing workbook for per-model calc.
- Burst absorb buffer: provision additional warm capacity to absorb 3x short bursts (targeting the 700 req/s peaks you called out). Practically that is +50-60% of base capacity in a warm pool (hot standby), not cold-started.
- Safety buffer: add 25% headroom for background system noise (network jitter, KV eviction during churn, autoscaler lag).
- Network/egress note: for private VPCs ensure 10Gbps per-node egress headroom if you expect concurrent large-model downloads or streaming to clients. We recommend testing egress shaping at 75% of that during canary.

Operational suggestions:
- Warm pool strategy: keep 1–2 GPUs per 4-GPU shard warmed (hot KV/cache primed).
- Canary schedule: 24 hours low-traffic validation (read-only inference tests) -> 48–72h ramp to 50% production traffic -> full cutover after SLA check.
- Failure mode: fallback to a smaller hosted Redwood model variant if private pool hits sustained 5-minute saturation; include routing policy for automated fallback.

Attaching a short runbook (buffer-allocation-runbook-v1.pdf) and a sizing spreadsheet (sizing-math-vivek.xlsx) with the per-model math. If you can share a sample p99 tail plot or 95/99 quantiles by time-of-day, we can refine the buffer math to reduce waste.

Next steps:
1) Ops: confirm egress rules and IP ranges for the canary window.
2) Anna: approve proposed warm pool + canary window dates.
3) We'll schedule a 1-hour run-through with your infra team to walk the runbook.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Vivek / team — internal notes and quick sizing delta after looking at the CSV and the initial calc Vivek shared. Quoting Vivek below for context:

On Sun, May 9, 2027 at 18:05 Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> Summary proposal (short):
> - Base steady capacity: size to sustain 200 req/s at target tail SLOs.

Sizing sketch (internal):
- Using the model latencies from the trace and assuming an H100-equivalent yields:
  • Steady: 4 nodes (H100-eq) to meet p99 target at 200 req/s.
  • Warm pool (burst absorb): +3 nodes kept hot to cover ~600–700 req/s 3–10 minute bursts (gives ~60% burst absorb).
  • Safety headroom: +1 node as margin for eviction/egress throttling (total recommended = 8 nodes).
- Alternative vertical: if they commit to quantized model variant (INT8) we can cut recommended steady to 3 nodes and warm pool to +2.

Canary proposal: 24h validation -> 48h stepped ramp (25%/50%/75%) -> 24h stabilization. Ops runbook linked in Vivek's attachment.

I'll attach the quick math sheet (sizing-math-vivek.xlsx) — use tab "zen_profile". Jon, Kim: please validate the network egress numbers (10Gbps/node) and confirm whether 1Gbps-per-CPU-host baseline will be OK during downloads.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference
